questions.stem: During mechanical ventilation, waste gas leaves the breathing system through which lettered valve?
questions.explanation: K is the ventilator relief (pressure relief) valve at the bellows. When the ventilator is in use, the APL (H) is out of circuit and waste gas leaves through the ventilator relief valve to the scavenger. A and B are the inspiratory and expiratory valves.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 19 (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: To confirm how much N2O remains, a tech weighs the cylinder at 7.1 kg. Which cylinder marking is needed to interpret that number?
questions.explanation: Because N2O pressure stays at 745 psig while liquid remains, contents are judged by weight: current weight minus the stamped tare weight equals the N2O left.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 9, 14 (PDF p. 5, 7)

questions.stem: Ten minutes after intubation, the provider realizes the ventilator was never switched on. Which findings fit? Select 3.
questions.explanation: Failure to initiate ventilation is the most common hypercarbia cause: the patient isn't breathing, so there's no chest rise, the bellows are still, CO2 builds, and SpO2 eventually falls. High pressure, a raised baseline, and a shark fin describe obstruction, rebreathing, and bronchospasm.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slides 20, 23 (PDF p. 10, 12)

questions.stem: Why does lowering fresh gas flow reduce the environmental impact of a volatile anesthetic?
options: It reduces compound A, which is a greenhouse gas
It lowers the agent's atmospheric lifetime
Less agent is vented through the scavenger to the atmosphere
questions.explanation: Scavenged agent is vented to the outside. Lower FGF means less fresh gas, and less agent, passes through the system per hour. Atmospheric lifetime is a property of the agent (sevo 1.1 yr, des 14 yr).
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 23 (PDF p. 12)

questions.stem: A medical air E-cylinder (625 L at 1900 psig) reads 1400 psig. About how much air remains?
questions.explanation: Compressed gas: 1400/1900 × 625 ≈ 460 L.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 7, 13 (PDF p. 4, 7)

questions.stem: During a power failure, a spontaneously breathing patient (MV 7 L/min) is placed on a Mapleson A running off a full O2 E-cylinder (about 660 L). About how long will the O2 last at the minimum recommended flow?
questions.explanation: Mapleson A needs FGF of at least 0.7 × MV = 4.9 L/min. 660 ÷ 4.9 ≈ 135 minutes. That's why Mapleson A is efficient for spontaneous breathing.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slides 21, 32 (PDF p. 11, 16); Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 13 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: Without scavenging, room sevoflurane measures 15 ppm. About what level would a properly working system produce, and would it meet NIOSH (no N2O in use)?
options: About 1.5 ppm; within the 2 ppm limit
About 1.5 ppm; exceeds the 0.5 ppm limit
questions.explanation: Scavenging cuts trace levels about 90%: 15 → 1.5 ppm. With no N2O, the halogenated limit is 2 ppm, so it's within. The 0.5 ppm limit applies only when N2O is also used.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 18 (PDF p. 9)

questions.stem: An oropharyngeal airway relieves obstruction mainly by lifting which labeled structure?
questions.explanation: A is the tongue, the main source of obstruction along with the soft palate. The OPA's caudally facing concave curve lifts it off the posterior pharynx. B is the vallecula, C the epiglottis, D the glossoepiglottic ligament.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slides 2, 5 (PDF p. 2, 5)

questions.stem: N2O is running and the provider turns the O2 flowmeter fully off. O2 supply pressure is normal. Which device prevents delivery of 100% N2O?
questions.explanation: The proportioning system links N2O flow to O2 flow at the flow control valves, so N2O falls as O2 is turned down. The fail-safe does nothing here because O2 supply pressure is normal.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 34, 45 (PDF p. 17, 23)

questions.stem: An O2 E-cylinder reads 1500 psig. About how long will it last at 6 L/min?
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 13 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: A patient with a minute ventilation of 9 L/min is transported on a Mapleson B. What fresh gas flow range prevents rebreathing?
questions.explanation: Mapleson B and C: 1.5-2.5 × MV = 13.5-22.5 L/min. 6.3 L/min would be the Mapleson A minimum (0.7 × MV).
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 21 (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: Right after the CO2 canister is changed, the leak check fails. Which causes are most likely? Select 2.
questions.explanation: Low-pressure leaks most commonly occur at the absorber: loose screws, worn gaskets, granules on gaskets, open petcock, or a poorly seated canister. Pipelines, cylinders, and the fail-safe are upstream of the low-pressure system.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 13 (PDF p. 7); Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 19 (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: Power fails with 25 minutes left in the case, and the battery typically lasts about 40 minutes. What is the right approach?
options: Set up TIVA and manual ventilation now in case the battery runs short
Turn off the monitors to save battery for the ventilator
Nothing; the battery will easily outlast the case
Increase fresh gas flow so the case finishes faster
questions.explanation: Battery life varies (about 40 minutes, some 1-2 hours, less if not fully charged). The lecture's plan is to set up alternatives within the window rather than gamble on the battery.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slides 25, 32 (PDF p. 13, 16)

questions.stem: Running on a limited O2 cylinder, which change stretches the supply the most while you arrange more O2?
options: Switch to manual (bag) ventilation with low fresh gas flow
Increase fresh gas flow to protect oxygenation
Switch the ventilator to a faster rate with smaller breaths
questions.explanation: The ventilator's driving gas comes from the O2 supply, so hand ventilation eliminates that use, and low FGF reduces the rest. Flushing wastes 35-75 L/min.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 5, 13 (PDF p. 3, 7); Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 23 (PDF p. 12)

questions.stem: Why does the lecture require full and empty cylinders to be stored separately?
options: So full cylinders don't transfill empty ones
So empty cylinders can be refilled in place
So an empty cylinder isn't grabbed in an emergency
questions.explanation: Separate storage (on nonflammable racks) keeps a provider from grabbing an empty cylinder during an emergency. Transfilling happens between open cylinders on a double yoke, not in storage.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 10 (PDF p. 5)

questions.stem: After an airway fire, why does the lecture include pouring saline into the airway and considering bronchoscopy? Select 2.
options: Bronchoscopy is done before stopping the gases
Bronchoscopy assesses injury and finds retained debris
Saline replaces the need to remove burning material
Saline raises FiO2 in the airway
questions.explanation: After pulling the tube and stopping gases, pour saline to put out residual fire, remove burning material, mask ventilate, then assess injury, consider bronchoscopy, and reintubate.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 36 (PDF p. 18)

questions.stem: An O2 E-cylinder reads 1200 psig. About how long will it supply a patient at 8 L/min?
questions.explanation: 1200/1900 × 660 L ≈ 417 L. 417 L ÷ 8 L/min ≈ 52 minutes. 150 minutes treats psig as liters divided by 8.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 13 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: The Tec 6 shows a 'no output' alarm during maintenance. What is the main clinical risk, and what should you do?
options: Hypoxemia; increase the O2 flow right away
Barotrauma; open the APL valve fully
Awareness; give IV anesthetic while troubleshooting
Overdose; turn off all fresh gas flow now
questions.explanation: No output means no des delivery, so the patient will lighten as expired agent falls. Cover with IV anesthetic while you troubleshoot (power, fill level, warm-up).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 64, 65 (PDF p. 32, 33); Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 32 (PDF p. 16)

questions.stem: The morning check shows the machine's backup O2 cylinder at 400 psig. What should happen before the first case?
options: Leave it; the pipeline makes the backup unnecessary
Replace it; a nearly empty backup is a hypoxemia hazard
Open it and leave it on to top up the pipeline
Record it; replace only if it drops below 100 psig
questions.explanation: Failure of the backup O2 reserve and an empty cylinder are highlighted hypoxemia hazards the machine check should catch. At 400 psig (about 140 L), the backup would last only minutes in a pipeline failure.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 19 (PDF p. 10); Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 13 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: Which reaction occurs FIRST when exhaled CO2 reaches soda lime?
options: CO2 combines with water to form carbonic acid
Carbonic acid reacts with calcium hydroxide
Sodium carbonate reacts with calcium hydroxide
questions.explanation: Sequence: CO2 + H2O → H2CO3; carbonic acid reacts rapidly with NaOH/KOH to form carbonates, water, and heat; then over minutes the carbonates react with Ca(OH)2 to form CaCO3 and regenerate NaOH.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 2 (PDF p. 1)

questions.stem: Mid-case, you realize the sevoflurane vaporizer was refilled with isoflurane. Agent analysis shows iso well above the dialed value. What is the FIRST step?
options: Lower the dial to half and continue
Keep going, since iso and sevo are equipotent
Drain it immediately while it's still mounted and on
Turn that vaporizer off and maintain anesthesia another way
questions.explanation: Iso's higher vapor pressure makes the sevo-calibrated vaporizer overdeliver, and iso is more potent. Stop delivery from that vaporizer first; draining and servicing happen after it's out of use.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 54, 70 (PDF p. 27, 35); Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 24 (PDF p. 12)

questions.stem: 240 V is applied across 1,200 ohms. What current flows?
questions.explanation: I = E/R = 240/1,200 = 0.2 A (200 mA). 288 comes from multiplying.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 26 (PDF p. 13)

questions.stem: Which of these are OXIDIZERS in the OR fire triangle? Select 2.
questions.explanation: The main OR oxidizers are air, O2, and N2O. Drapes and alcohol prep are fuel, the ESU is an ignition source, and helium isn't listed as an oxidizer.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 33 (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: Running on cylinder O2 only, the cylinder gradually empties while N2O is on. In what order do things happen?
options: O2 supply alarm → N2O proportionally reduced → N2O stopped
Nothing changes until the cylinder reads 0 psig
N2O stopped → O2 supply alarm → N2O reduced
N2O reduced → N2O stopped → O2 supply alarm
questions.explanation: As O2 supply pressure falls, the low-pressure alarm warns first, then the fail-safe proportionally reduces other gases (below about 25-30 psig) and finally stops them (below about 20).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 33, 34 (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: A patient on 2 L/min nasal cannula is transported with an O2 E-cylinder reading 800 psig. About how long is available?
questions.explanation: 800/1900 × 660 ≈ 278 L. 278 ÷ 2 ≈ 139 minutes. 400 would treat psig as liters.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 13 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: Under the same desiccated conditions, which absorbent produces more CO?
questions.explanation: CO production is greater with barium hydroxide lime than with soda lime, and it rises with desiccation, temperature, and agent concentration.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 7 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: On this variable bypass vaporizer, the dial is turned from 1% to 3%. Flow through which numbered path increases?
questions.explanation: Path 2 carries fresh gas into the vaporizing chamber. Turning the dial up directs more fresh gas there, lowering the splitting ratio. Path 1 is the bypass, and 4 is the outflow at the dialed concentration.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 53, 54 (PDF p. 27)

questions.stem: Which temperature facts are correct? Select 2.
options: CO2 is stored as gas only
Medical air is liquid in an E-cylinder at room temperature
questions.explanation: O2's critical temperature is −118.6 °C (it boils at −183 °C at 1 atm). N2O's critical temperature is about 36 °C (it boils at −88 °C), so it's liquid in an E-cylinder at room temperature. Air is a gas; CO2 is liquid/gas.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 11, 14 (PDF p. 6, 7)

questions.stem: Which tube feature does the ISO standard address that directly affects ventilation if the bevel is blocked against the tracheal wall?
questions.explanation: The Murphy eye is on the ISO list (with ID/OD, distance markers, toxicity, bevel, radius of curvature). It provides an alternate path for gas if the bevel opening is occluded.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 7 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: When lettered component G is switched from bag to ventilator, which lettered valve is taken out of the circuit?
questions.explanation: G is the manual/automatic selector. Switching to ventilator connects the bellows (J) and takes the reservoir bag (I) and APL (H) out of circuit, so adjusting the APL does nothing during mechanical ventilation.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 19 (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: Which ignition source is easy to overlook because it isn't in the surgeon's hand?
options: A fiberoptic light cord end resting on the drapes
The ETT cuff and its pilot balloon
The BP cuff on the upper arm
The pulse oximeter probe on a finger
questions.explanation: The lecture lists the ESU, lasers, and the ends of fiberoptic light cords as ignition sources. A light cord left on the drapes can ignite them.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 33 (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: A tech completes the morning check; the provider doesn't confirm it. Mid-case, the pipeline fails and the O2 cylinder turns out to be closed and nearly empty. Which aggravating factor best describes the provider's role?
questions.explanation: The lecture says to confirm the machine check was actually done, especially when delegated. An unverified check that missed an empty backup is failure to check equipment.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slides 18, 19 (PDF p. 9, 10)

questions.stem: Sevo at 3% with 1 L/min FGF versus des at 6% with 1 L/min FGF. How does hourly liquid use compare?
options: Des uses twice as much (18 vs 9 mL/hr)
Des uses six times as much
Sevo uses twice as much (18 vs 9 mL/hr)
questions.explanation: mL/hr = vol% × FGF × 3: sevo 3 × 1 × 3 = 9; des 6 × 1 × 3 = 18. The formula scales directly with the dialed percentage.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 50, 52 (PDF p. 25, 26)

questions.stem: A copper kettle with isoflurane (vapor pressure 240 mmHg) receives 100 mL/min of O2. The saturated gas joins 5 L/min of fresh gas. Roughly what concentration is delivered?
questions.explanation: Saturated gas is 240/760 ≈ 32% vapor, so vapor added = 100 × 240/(760 − 240) ≈ 46 mL/min. 46 mL in about 5,146 mL total ≈ 0.9%. The kettle isn't concentration-calibrated, which is why these calculations are required.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 50, 74 (PDF p. 25, 37)

questions.stem: Which OR ventilation setups meet the lecture's air exchange requirements? Select 2.
options: Recirculating, 17 exchanges per hour with 3 fresh
Recirculating, 20 exchanges per hour with 1 fresh plus filters
Recirculating, 14 exchanges per hour with 4 fresh
Recirculating, 21 exchanges per hour with 2 fresh
questions.explanation: Nonrecirculating systems should provide 15 or more exchanges per hour. Recirculating systems need 15-21 per hour with at least 3 fresh outside air; filters don't remove anesthetic gases.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 16, 17 (PDF p. 8, 9)

questions.stem: Which numbered components on this machine roadmap sit in the intermediate-pressure system? Select 3.
questions.explanation: The intermediate system runs from the first-stage regulator and pipeline inlets to the flow control valves. It contains the fail-safe (1) and the second-stage O2 and N2O regulators (2, 3). The pressure relief valve (4) and outlet check valve (5) sit downstream of the vaporizers in the low-pressure system.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 5, 26, 76 (PDF p. 3, 13, 38)

questions.stem: A paralyzed patient is ventilated through a Mapleson A for transport. Why is that a poor choice?
options: Mapleson A needs no fresh gas during controlled ventilation
Mapleson A's tubing is too short for adults
Mapleson A can't connect to an ETT
Mapleson A is designed for spontaneous breathing; B or C suits controlled ventilation
questions.explanation: The lecture says the Mapleson A should be used only with spontaneously breathing patients. For controlled ventilation, B and C work, since the patient isn't doing the extra work of breathing, with FGF 1.5-2.5 × MV.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 21 (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: A patient with an implanted pacemaker needs a procedure with electrocautery. Which ESU concern does the lecture specifically name?
questions.explanation: The lecture lists implanted pacemakers among devices affected by ESU interference, along with ECG, cardiac output computers, and pulse oximeters.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 31 (PDF p. 16)

questions.stem: An edentulous patient is hard to mask ventilate because the cheeks collapse and air leaks around the mask. What helps most?
options: Insert an oral airway to restore the seal
Use a smaller mask pressed harder
questions.explanation: The lecture notes an OPA improves bag-mask seal in edentulous patients, restoring structure and lifting the tongue. More flow doesn't fix a leaking seal.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slides 4, 5 (PDF p. 4, 5)

questions.stem: Flows are O2 1.5 L/min, N2O 3 L/min, and air 3 L/min. What is the delivered FiO2?
questions.explanation: O2 delivered = 1.5 + 0.21 × 3 = 2.13 L of 7.5 L total ≈ 28%. The 33% value is O2 as a share of O2 + N2O only, which is what the proportioner checks.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 45 (PDF p. 23)

questions.stem: Which statements about the O2 flush are correct? Select 3.
options: It adds anesthetic agent from the vaporizer
It bypasses the flowmeters and vaporizers
It works with both pipeline and cylinder unavailable
It passes through the second-stage regulator to the flowmeters
questions.explanation: The flush sends 35-75 L/min at 40-50 psi from the intermediate system directly to the CGO, bypassing flowmeters and vaporizers (so it dilutes agent). It needs an O2 source: pipeline or first-stage regulator.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 36, 37 (PDF p. 18, 19)

questions.stem: Where should the ESU return pad go for a left knee arthroplasty?
options: On the left thigh, close to the site
On the chest, near the ECG pads
On the right shoulder, far from the site
questions.explanation: Place the return plate as close as possible to the operative site (with good skin contact) and ECG pads as far away as feasible, keeping the current path short.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 31 (PDF p. 16)

questions.stem: The O2 flush delivers 35-75 L/min. About how much gas enters the circuit during a 1-second press, and why does that matter during inspiration?
options: About 0.6-1.25 L, more than a typical tidal volume, risking barotrauma
About 6-12 L, enough to rupture the reservoir bag
About 0.1 L, only enough to dilute agent
questions.explanation: 35-75 L/min ÷ 60 ≈ 0.6-1.25 L per second. Delivered on top of a 500 mL breath, that's a large volume at 40-50 psi source pressure, the basis of the flush's barotrauma risk.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 36, 37 (PDF p. 18, 19)

questions.stem: Under which condition can O2 be kept as a liquid in a bulk storage tank?
options: At room temperature under enough pressure
questions.explanation: −118.6 °C is O2's critical temperature, the highest temperature at which pressure can liquefy it. Room temperature is far above it, so no pressure keeps O2 liquid there. −183 °C is the boiling point at 1 atm, not a requirement for storage under pressure.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 11 (PDF p. 6)

questions.stem: Which conditions worsen the vaporizer pumping effect? Select 3.
questions.explanation: Pumping comes from retrograde pressure: PPV and O2 flush, worse at low FGF and low liquid levels. An outlet check valve minimizes it, and high FGF and full vaporizers lessen it.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 72 (PDF p. 36)

questions.stem: During MAC for a scalp procedure, O2 runs at 4 L/min by cannula under a tented drape near the cautery site. Which prevention step addresses the specific hazard?
options: Add N2O to lower the fraction of O2 under the drape
Tuck the drape tightly around the head and face
Keep O2 from pooling under drapes; use the lowest O2 flow tolerated
Increase O2 flow to 10 L/min to dilute any vapors
questions.explanation: O2 trapped under drapes near an ignition source is the classic MAC fire setup. Configure drapes to avoid oxidizer buildup and keep O2 as low as clinically possible; N2O is also an oxidizer.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 35 (PDF p. 18)

questions.stem: If the numbered component 3 failed, what function would be lost?
options: Matching vapor delivery to fresh gas back pressure
Heating the liquid desflurane to 39 °C in the sump
Letting the provider select the output concentration
Separating the diluent path from the outflow port
questions.explanation: Component 3 is the differential pressure transducer. It compares the vapor and diluent circuits and adjusts valve 1 so vapor delivery tracks fresh gas flow. The heater warms the sump, and the dial (valve 2) sets concentration.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 62, 63 (PDF p. 31, 32)

questions.stem: Which agents produce essentially NO carbon monoxide with desiccated absorbent? Select 2.
questions.explanation: CO comes from agents with a difluoromethyl (-O-CHF2) group: des > enflurane > iso. Sevoflurane and halothane lack it (sevo's concern is compound A).
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 7 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: A 2-hour case runs isoflurane at 1.5% on 4 L/min. What volume of liquid iso is consumed?
questions.explanation: mL/hr = vol% × FGF × 3 = 1.5 × 4 × 3 = 18 mL/hr. Two hours: 36 mL.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 52 (PDF p. 26)

questions.stem: Which landmark sequence locates the cricothyroid membrane for emergency access?
options: From the sternal notch up about two tracheal rings
From the hyoid bone down to the first soft gap below it
From the thyroid prominence down to the gap just above the cricoid
From the cricoid ring down to the next soft gap
questions.explanation: The CTM spans from the inferior border of the thyroid cartilage to the superior edge of the cricoid. Moving down from the thyroid prominence, it's the gap just above the cricoid; below the cricoid are tracheal rings.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 15 (PDF p. 15)

questions.stem: During thyroidectomy with the drapes over the face, the exhaled volume suddenly falls and pressures drop. What is the FIRST check?
options: The ETT-circuit connection under the drapes
The O2 cylinder pressure on the machine
The vaporizer filler cap on the manifold
questions.explanation: Leaks and disconnections are especially common in neck surgery when the drape covers the face and the tube connection comes loose. Low pressure and low volume point to a disconnection.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 23 (PDF p. 12)

questions.stem: Which flowmeter design features protect specifically against turning the wrong knob? Select 2.
options: O2 positioned last in the sequence
Green color coding of the O2 knob
questions.explanation: Color and touch coding (a larger, fluted, green O2 knob) give visual and tactile checks against turning the wrong knob. O2-last placement protects against leaks, not knob errors.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 40, 41 (PDF p. 20, 21)

questions.stem: Which conditions promote compound A formation? Select 3.
questions.explanation: Compound A comes from sevoflurane and rises with warmer, drier absorbent, higher agent concentration, and lower FGF. Moisture promotes its breakdown, and desflurane forms CO, not compound A.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 6 (PDF p. 3)

questions.stem: Why is only one washer used between the cylinder valve and the hanger yoke?
options: Two washers overheat as gas rushes through the valve
Washers are single-use items for infection control reasons
Extra washers can keep the pins from engaging and cause leaks
A second washer blocks the yoke check valve from opening
questions.explanation: PISS depends on the pins seating fully in the valve holes. Extra washers add thickness, so pins may not engage (defeating PISS) and the seal can leak. One washer only.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 18, 19 (PDF p. 9, 10)

questions.stem: A lot of medical O2 is found to contain impurities and must be pulled from use nationwide. Which agency handles this?
questions.explanation: FDA oversees medical gas purity and recalls (and anesthesia checkout). DOT covers cylinder manufacture, filling, labeling, and transport; OSHA covers worker exposure; ASTM writes machine component standards.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 4 (PDF p. 2)

questions.stem: Why does the lecture recommend avoiding N2O as a carrier gas?
options: It shortens the life of the CO2 absorbent canister
It increases compound A formation in the absorber
It raises the NIOSH halogenated exposure limit
It lasts up to 114 years, and carrier use means large volumes
questions.explanation: N2O has the longest atmospheric life (up to 114 years), and as a carrier it's delivered in large volumes. The lecture recommends avoiding it as a carrier and reserving it for cases where it reduces morbidity.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 22, 23 (PDF p. 11, 12)

questions.stem: What component sits immediately downstream of each cylinder hanger yoke?
options: The fail-safe valve in the N2O line
The O2 flowmeter and needle valve
questions.explanation: Immediately distal to the hanger yoke is the regulator that drops variable cylinder pressure to about 45 psi before gas enters the intermediate system.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 9, 24 (PDF p. 5, 12); Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 9 (PDF p. 5)

questions.stem: Which numbered path carries gas that is fully saturated with anesthetic vapor?
questions.explanation: Path 3 is gas leaving the vaporizing chamber, saturated with vapor (sevo about 21% at 20 °C). It then mixes with bypass gas (path 1), which is never exposed to agent, to produce the dialed concentration at the outflow (path 4).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 53, 57 (PDF p. 27, 29)

questions.stem: Which components operate at just above atmospheric pressure? Select 3.
questions.explanation: Low pressure: downstream of the flow control valves (flowmeters, vaporizers, check valve, CGO), slightly above atmospheric. Second-stage regulators, pipeline inlets, and the fail-safe are intermediate.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 39, 76 (PDF p. 20, 38)

questions.stem: Which statements about the common gas outlet are correct? Select 3.
options: It has a 22 mm external diameter
It uses a 30 mm conical fitting
It uses a 19 mm conical fitting
Two outlets are required for backup
It has a 15 mm internal diameter
A machine may have only one
questions.explanation: The standard requires one CGO with a 15 mm ID (female) and 22 mm OD (male). 19 and 30 mm conical fittings are reserved for scavenging.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 15 (PDF p. 8)

questions.stem: Which numbered component creates back pressure in proportion to fresh gas flow, which the vaporizer uses to match vapor delivery?
questions.explanation: Component 4 is the fixed resistance (gas circuit restrictor) in the diluent flow. Higher FGF creates higher back pressure there; the transducer (3) senses it and opens valve 1 so vapor pressure matches, keeping the dialed concentration.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 62, 63 (PDF p. 31, 32)

questions.stem: With a splitting ratio of about 25:1 at 2 L/min total fresh gas, roughly how much fresh gas enters the sevoflurane chamber?
questions.explanation: A 25:1 ratio splits the flow into 26 parts: 2,000 ÷ 26 ≈ 77 mL/min to the chamber and about 1,920 mL/min through the bypass. That's the lecture's 1% sevo example.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 55 (PDF p. 28)

questions.stem: A machine has only an Aladin cassette and a Tec 6 mounted. After the battery is exhausted, what inhalational options remain?
options: None; both need power, so switch to TIVA
Either, if fresh gas flow is increased
The Aladin, because cassettes are mechanical
The Tec 6, because its sump stays pressurized
questions.explanation: Desflurane vaporizers (Tec 6, D-Vapor) and electronic vaporizers (Aladin) can't deliver agent without electrical power. Only conventional mechanical vaporizers work on emergency O2.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 32 (PDF p. 16); Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 66 (PDF p. 33)

questions.stem: The O2 pipeline is contaminated with nitrogen, and a resident presses the O2 flush to 'give more oxygen.' What happens?
options: Pure O2 is delivered, since the flush bypasses the pipeline
The flush switches to the cylinder automatically
More contaminated gas is delivered, since the flush draws from the pipeline
questions.explanation: The flush takes O2 from the pipeline (or cylinder regulator) and bypasses only the flowmeters and vaporizers. With the pipeline preferred and contaminated, the flush delivers contaminated gas at high flow. Disconnect the pipeline and open the cylinder.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 36, 46 (PDF p. 18, 23)

questions.stem: Monday's first case is a long, low-flow sevoflurane anesthetic, and the canister feels warm and dry. What is the concern and best response?
options: Nothing; sevo is safe with dry absorbent
questions.explanation: Sevo with warm, dry absorbent at low flow promotes compound A. Desiccated absorbent shouldn't be used with either agent, and des would add CO risk.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 6, 7 (PDF p. 3, 4)

questions.stem: Regurgitated gastric fluid would first enter the LMA Supreme's drain channel at which numbered point?
questions.explanation: Point 6 is the drain tube opening at the cuff tip, which sits at the upper esophagus. The channel runs up to the drain tube (1), which also allows gastric tube passage. Point 2 is the airway tube with its 15 mm connector.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 14)

questions.stem: A Macintosh blade is placed correctly in the vallecula, but the epiglottis doesn't lift. Which structure isn't being tensioned effectively?
questions.explanation: The Mac works indirectly: pressure in the vallecula tensions the glossoepiglottic ligament, which lifts the epiglottis. If that fails (e.g., a long floppy epiglottis), a Miller can lift the epiglottis directly.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 11 (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: An isoflurane case also uses N2O. Sampling finds iso 0.4 ppm and N2O 22 ppm TWA. Are these compliant with NIOSH?
questions.explanation: With N2O in use, the halogenated limit is 0.5 ppm, and N2O's limit is 25 ppm TWA. 0.4 and 22 are both under.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 10 (PDF p. 5)
questions.supp: The 0.5 ppm combined-use limit comes from NIOSH's 1977 recommendation; slide 10 lists only 2 ppm and 25 ppm.

questions.stem: During spontaneous or manually assisted ventilation, which lettered valve sends excess gas to the scavenger?
questions.explanation: H is the APL (pop-off) valve, the exit for waste gas during spontaneous or manual ventilation. K is used during mechanical ventilation, and G is the manual/automatic selector.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 19 (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: A new O2 cylinder hisses loudly when opened on the yoke. What's the most likely cause?
options: Missing or damaged washer at the yoke
questions.explanation: The plastic washer and T-handle seal the cylinder to the yoke. A missing, damaged, or doubled washer leaks at the connection. Close the valve and replace the washer (one only).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 18, 19 (PDF p. 9, 10); Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 7 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: After the last case, a tech flushes the circuit with O2 and squeezes the bag into the room to 'clear it out.' What's the problem?
options: Nothing, since the patient has already left
It desiccates the absorbent before the next morning
It damages the APL valve's spring mechanism
Anesthetic left in the circuit is released into the room
questions.explanation: Flushing or emptying the breathing circuit into room air spills whatever agent remains, a technique error on the lecture's list. Separately, leaving high flows running overnight desiccates the absorbent.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: Which statements about grounding are correct? Select 2.
options: Ungrounded OR power increases macroshock risk
Home equipment must always be grounded
questions.explanation: In the OR, power is usually ungrounded, isolating current from ground potential for added macroshock protection, while equipment is grounded. At home, power is grounded and equipment may or may not be.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slides 29, 30 (PDF p. 15)

questions.stem: Pipeline O2 has failed, but the O2 cylinder was opened promptly. Does the O2 flush work?
options: Yes, but only at half flow
No; the flush only works from the pipeline
No; the fail-safe blocks the flush
Yes; it draws from the first-stage regulator
questions.explanation: The flush opens O2 from the pipeline or the first-stage (cylinder) regulator directly to the CGO. With the cylinder open, it has a source. With both pipeline and cylinder unavailable, it gives nothing.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 24, 36 (PDF p. 12, 18)

questions.stem: The ESU return pad is placed over a hairy, bony area and partly lifts during the case. What risk does this create?
options: A burn under the pad from current concentrating on a small area
Loss of ECG signal caused by the lifted pad
The ESU stops working with no warning at all
Ventricular fibrillation from the ESU current
questions.explanation: The pad works by spreading current over a large area. Poor contact shrinks that area and concentrates current, which burns. The ESU's radiofrequency current doesn't cause V-fib.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 31 (PDF p. 16)

questions.stem: Des at 8% on 1.5 L/min for a 90-minute case consumes about how much liquid?
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 52 (PDF p. 26)

questions.stem: A machine uses electronically controlled flowmeters set through a computer interface. Why does the lecture's power-failure plan matter especially here?
options: Electronic flow control needs power; only emergency O2 remains after
Electronic flowmeters work more accurately on battery power
Mechanical vaporizers depend on the electronic flow controller
The proportioning system switches to mechanical on battery
questions.explanation: Electronic flow controllers use solenoid-controlled orifices set through the workstation computer. Once the battery is exhausted, only basic functions like emergency O2 remain, so plan alternatives early.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slides 12, 32 (PDF p. 6, 16); Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 35 (PDF p. 18)

questions.stem: A zone valve closure leaves you on a cylinder reading 500 psig (about 174 L). The ventilator's driving gas is O2, and total O2 use (fresh gas plus drive gas) is about 8 L/min. About how long do you have?
questions.explanation: 174 L ÷ 8 L/min ≈ 22 minutes. The roadmap shows the ventilator driving gas taken from the O2 supply, so mechanical ventilation consumes cylinder O2 on top of fresh gas flow.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 5, 13 (PDF p. 3, 7); Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 4 (PDF p. 2)

questions.stem: A device delivers 1,000 W for 0.2 seconds. How much energy is that?
questions.explanation: Joules = watts × seconds = 1,000 × 0.2 = 200 J.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 26 (PDF p. 13)

questions.stem: In a small infant, an HME, a long elbow, and an extension are added between the Y-piece and the ETT. ETCO2 climbs despite unchanged settings. Why?
options: Added apparatus dead space causes rebreathing
questions.explanation: Increased apparatus dead space is a delivery-system hypercarbia hazard. In a small patient, a few added connectors can be a large fraction of tidal volume.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 20 (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: The O2 pipeline reads 48 psig and the O2 cylinder is closed. Which source is supplying the machine?
questions.explanation: With the cylinder closed, the pipeline is the only source, and 48 psig is well above the fail-safe range. It's slightly below the usual 50-55 psi, worth reporting, but still supplying normally.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 4 (PDF p. 2); Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 33 (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: A medical air E-cylinder (625 L full at 1900 psig) reads 950 psig. About how long will it last at 5 L/min?
questions.explanation: Air is a compressed gas, so contents fall linearly with pressure: half pressure ≈ 312 L. 312 ÷ 5 ≈ 62 minutes.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 7, 13 (PDF p. 4, 7)

questions.stem: A vaporizer is being refilled between cases. Which practice limits room contamination?
options: Leave the filler cap loose until the next case
Fill quickly with the bottle tilted to save time
Fill with the vaporizer turned on to purge air
Use the key fill adapter and avoid spills
questions.explanation: Spills while filling vaporizers are one of the technique errors that release anesthetic into the room. Key fill adapters limit spills and misfilling, and the cap should be tightened.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: Which anesthetic agent dosage problems does the hazards lecture list? Select 3.
options: Crossed hospital O2 and N2O pipelines
Simultaneous use of more than one vaporizer
Excessive O2 flush use during ventilation
Liquid agent in the fresh gas piping
Exhausted CO2 absorbent in the canister
questions.explanation: The slide lists liquid agent in the fresh gas piping, concentration dial design, incorrect filling, and simultaneous use of more than one vaporizer. Absorbent exhaustion and crossed pipelines are hypercarbia and hypoxemia hazards.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 24 (PDF p. 12)

questions.stem: Where does OSHA recommend waste anesthetic gas scavenging?
questions.explanation: OSHA enacts and enforces standards and recommends scavenging in all anesthetizing locations. TJC goes further, requiring active scavenging methods.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 10 (PDF p. 5)

questions.stem: Which features describe the Tec 6 desflurane vaporizer? Select 3.
options: Uses wicks to saturate fresh gas
Routes part of the fresh gas through the sump
Pressurizes the sump to about 2 atm
Uses a bimetallic strip for compensation
questions.explanation: The Tec 6 heats des to 39 °C, pressurizes it to about 2 atm (1500 mmHg), and needs electricity. Fresh gas never enters the sump; vapor is injected. Wicks and bimetallic strips belong to variable bypass designs.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 60, 61, 62 (PDF p. 30, 31)

questions.stem: Which numbered component connects to the breathing circuit elbow?
questions.explanation: Component 2 is the airway tube with its standard 15 mm connector, the same size that fits circuit elbows and ETTs. Component 1 is the separate drain tube for gastric access.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 14)

questions.stem: During laryngoscopy, only the epiglottis tip is visible. The lecture's equipment options include which device to help guide the tube?
questions.explanation: The Eschmann introducer is an intubating stylet placed through the glottis first, then the tube is loaded over it. The other devices don't guide intubation.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slides 10, 11 (PDF p. 10, 11)

questions.stem: Before the surgeon enters the trachea with cautery during a tracheostomy, what should anesthesia do?
options: Increase fresh gas flow to flush the trachea of O2
Turn on N2O so that the O2 concentration falls lower
Raise FiO2 to 100% to build a safety margin first
Lower FiO2 as tolerated, avoid N2O, and coordinate with the surgeon
questions.explanation: Oxidizer and ignition source are about to meet in the airway. The prevention list: keep O2 as low as clinically possible, avoid N2O, and notify the surgeon when oxidizer and ignition source are in proximity.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 35 (PDF p. 18)

questions.stem: N2O is set at 6 L/min on a machine whose proportioning system holds O2 at 25% or more of O2 + N2O. What is the minimum O2 flow?
questions.explanation: O2/(O2 + 6) = 0.25 → O2 = 2 L/min (2 of 8 L total).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 45 (PDF p. 23)

questions.stem: During spontaneous ventilation, which problems cause HIGH breathing-circuit pressure? Select 3.
options: Kinked tubing between the APL and scavenging interface
A leak in the breathing circuit tubing
APL valve opened fully to the scavenger
questions.explanation: Slide 23: high pressure during spontaneous ventilation can come from a partly or fully closed APL, kinked or occluded tubing between the APL and scavenging interface, or a malfunctioning interface positive-pressure relief valve. Disconnections and leaks lower pressure.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 23 (PDF p. 12)

questions.stem: Which are OBJECTIVE measures of bag-mask ventilation adequacy? Select 3.
questions.explanation: Objective measures: sustained SpO2, waveform exhaled CO2, peak airway pressure, exhaled tidal volume. Chest movement and gas leak are the lecture's clinical signs, and fog is a visual cue.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 4 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: About how much CO2 can a 500 g charge of soda lime absorb?
questions.explanation: 100 g absorbs about 26 L, so 500 g absorbs about 130 L.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 2 (PDF p. 1)

questions.stem: Which E-cylinders hold compressed GAS only (contents proportional to pressure)? Select 3.
questions.explanation: O2, air, and helium are stored as gas, so pressure tracks contents. N2O and CO2 are liquid/gas, holding constant pressure until the liquid is gone.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 7 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: Twenty minutes into a 3-hour desflurane anesthetic, building power fails. What is the priority?
options: Wait for the low-battery alarm, then switch to TIVA
Increase the desflurane dial to deepen the patient before power runs out
Start a TIVA infusion and prepare manual ventilation now, while the battery lasts
Ask the surgeon to finish within 40 minutes
questions.explanation: The battery lasts about 40 minutes to 2 hours, and the Tec 6 needs power. The lecture says to use the window to set up TIVA and a Mapleson (or manual ventilation) so the patient is covered well before the battery is gone.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slides 25, 32 (PDF p. 13, 16)

questions.stem: Which devices respond to O2 SUPPLY PRESSURE? Select 2.
questions.explanation: The fail-safe and the O2 supply low-pressure alarm both respond to supply pressure. The proportioner responds to flow settings, the analyzer to concentration, and PISS is mechanical indexing.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 33, 34 (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: A provider answering texts misses a circuit disconnection until SpO2 falls. Which aggravating factors apply?
questions.explanation: The lecture says inattention and distraction are increasingly common causes, often from phone use or conversation.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slides 18, 23 (PDF p. 9, 12)

questions.stem: Six months after adding battery checks to the machine checklist, the department reviews whether power-related events have decreased. Which risk management step is this?
questions.explanation: The steps: define problems, estimate likelihood, weigh resources, apply solutions, monitor. Reviewing results after a change is monitoring.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 16 (PDF p. 8)

questions.stem: During an N2O-only sedation, the case-average N2O level measures 40 ppm, but the 8-hour shift average is 15 ppm. How does this compare with the NIOSH limit?
options: Within it; N2O alone has no limit
Within it; the 8-hour average is what counts
Exceeds it only if a halogenated agent is also used
Exceeds it; the limit is a TWA during anesthetic administration
questions.explanation: NIOSH's N2O limit is 25 ppm TWA during the anesthetic administration, not averaged over the whole shift. 40 ppm during the case exceeds it.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 10 (PDF p. 5)

questions.stem: The absorbent was purple at the end of yesterday's cases and looks white this morning. What is the correct action?
options: Watch it; change it only if it turns purple again
Use it; overnight rest restored its capacity
Use it only at high fresh gas flow
Change it; the color regenerated, but capacity didn't
questions.explanation: Ethyl violet can fade back to white after rest (regeneration), but the absorbent's capacity isn't restored. That's a core reason the lecture says indicator color isn't to be relied on.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 4 (PDF p. 2)

questions.stem: Which component-to-pressure-system pairings are correct? Select 2.
questions.explanation: High pressure: yoke, cylinder gauge, first-stage regulator. Intermediate: pipeline inlets, second-stage regulators, fail-safe, flush, flow control valves. Low: flowmeters, vaporizers, check valve, common gas outlet.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 26, 39, 76 (PDF p. 13, 20, 38)

questions.stem: A fluid warmer draws 12 A at 120 V. How much power does it use?
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 26 (PDF p. 13)

questions.stem: Flames appear on the drapes near the patient's face during MAC with O2 by cannula. What is the anesthesia provider's FIRST step?
questions.explanation: Fire on the patient: turn off gases, remove drapes and burning materials, extinguish, then assess, including smoke inhalation. The oxidizer is anesthesia's element to remove first.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 37 (PDF p. 19)

questions.stem: On this LMA Supreme, which numbered component protects the airway tube if the patient bites down?
questions.explanation: Component 4 is the integrated bite block. 1 is the drain tube, 3 the fixation tab, and 5 the modified cuff.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 14)

questions.stem: Which sequence matches the lecture's fix for a tipped variable bypass vaporizer?
options: Drain, refill immediately, then recalibrate the concentration dial
Refill, run the highest setting, then drain once analysis reads zero
Run the lowest setting for 30 min, then drain and refill it
Drain, run highest setting at high FGF ~30 min, refill when analysis reads zero
questions.explanation: Tipping puts liquid in the bypass. Drain the vaporizer, run it at the highest setting with high FGF for about 30 minutes to clear the bypass, and refill once expired gas analysis no longer detects agent.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 71 (PDF p. 36)

questions.stem: A facial procedure needs cautery near the airway, and the patient can't tolerate low FiO2. Which airway plan lowers fire risk most?
options: Secure the airway with a cuffed ETT instead of open O2
Use a face mask tucked under the surgical drapes
Use high-flow nasal cannula O2 during cautery
Add N2O so less O2 is needed at the face
questions.explanation: The lecture singles out open O2 delivery (mask, cannula) near the airway as the danger. A sealed airway keeps oxidizer inside the circuit instead of pooling under drapes near the ignition source. N2O is also an oxidizer.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 35 (PDF p. 18)

questions.stem: A brown E-cylinder (500 L full at 1600 psi) reads 800 psi. About how much gas remains?
questions.explanation: Brown = helium, a compressed gas stored at 1600 psi with 500 L when full. Half the pressure means about half the contents: 250 L.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 7 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: A pregnant circulating nurse is assigned to a case planned with an LMA and volatile maintenance. Which change most reduces her exposure?
options: Ensure a good seal or use a cuffed ETT; no gas while disconnected
Use a smaller LMA to reduce apparatus dead space
Increase fresh gas flow to dilute any leaked agent
Switch to N2O as the carrier gas for the case
questions.explanation: LMAs commonly vent more gas into the room than cuffed tubes, and technique errors cause most contamination. The lecture flags pregnant staff because of the 1974 findings. N2O adds exposure.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 9, 14 (PDF p. 5, 7); Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 14)

questions.stem: After the workstation battery dies, how can a paralyzed, intubated patient still be ventilated?
options: Ventilation isn't possible until power returns
The ventilator continues on reserve pneumatics indefinitely
The O2 flush can be pulsed to ventilate
Manually, with a bag on emergency O2 (circle bag or Mapleson)
questions.explanation: Battery failure stops the ventilator, monitors, and alarms, but emergency O2 remains. Ventilate by hand, with a Mapleson set up during the battery window as the lecture recommends.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slides 25, 32 (PDF p. 13, 16)

questions.stem: Right after a new absorber canister is installed, peak pressure is very high and no gas flows. What should be checked?
options: Packaging or wrap left on the canister
questions.explanation: Failure to completely remove plastic wrapping from breathing system components is a reported cause of total occlusion. The machine check should catch it.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 22 (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: Inspired CO2 is rising from an exhausted canister that can't be replaced for several minutes. Which temporary measure reduces rebreathing?
options: Switch to a higher sevoflurane concentration
questions.explanation: The absorber is essential at low flow; without effective absorption, fresh gas flow is what washes CO2 out. Raising FGF limits rebreathing until the canister is changed (the hazards lecture lists inadequate FGF without absorption as a hypercarbia hazard).
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 4, 8 (PDF p. 2, 4); Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 20 (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: Exhaled gas leaving the patient passes through which lettered valve before reaching the absorbent?
questions.explanation: B is the expiratory unidirectional valve on the limb returning from the patient; E is the absorbent. A is the inspiratory valve sending gas to the patient.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 8, 19 (PDF p. 4, 10)

questions.stem: A patient with an LMA Supreme begins to regurgitate. Which feature allows gastric contents to be vented or suctioned away from the airway?
questions.explanation: The LMA Supreme's separate drain tube runs from an opening at the cuff tip, allowing gastric drainage or passage of a gastric tube.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 14); CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: Which sequence describes temperature compensation in a variable bypass vaporizer during a long case?
options: Liquid warms → vapor pressure falls → strip bends → more gas through the chamber
Liquid cools → strip heats the sump → vapor pressure is restored
Liquid cools → vapor pressure rises → strip bends → more gas through the bypass
Liquid cools → vapor pressure falls → strip bends → more gas through the chamber
questions.explanation: Vaporization cools the liquid, lowering vapor pressure and output. The bimetallic strip responds by sending more fresh gas through the chamber (changing the splitting ratio) so output stays at the dial. Only the Tec 6 uses a heater.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 56 (PDF p. 28)

questions.stem: A rushed 0600 case starts with an unchecked machine; during the case, the provider is chatting with the surgical team and misses a slowly falling FiO2. Which aggravating factors are present? Select 3.
questions.explanation: Rushing is haste, skipping the check is failure to check equipment, and conversation is distraction. Nothing in the scenario suggests unfamiliarity, inexperience, or a design defect. Most events are multifactorial like this.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slides 17, 18 (PDF p. 9)

questions.stem: Using the lecture's property table, which agent has the highest percentage metabolized?
questions.explanation: Halothane is metabolized far more (about 15-40%) than sevoflurane (a few percent), isoflurane, or desflurane (minimal).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 50 (PDF p. 25)

questions.stem: The O2 flowmeter reads 3 L/min, pipeline pressures are normal, and inspired O2 keeps falling. Which causes fit? Select 2.
options: A crack in the O2 flowmeter tube
Nitrogen or another gas in the O2 pipeline
questions.explanation: Normal pressures with falling FiO2 point to gas composition or O2 lost after metering: contamination (crossed pipelines, nitrogen) or a leak in the O2 flowmeter. The fail-safe only acts on low pressure, and flushing adds O2.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 46, 48 (PDF p. 23, 24)

questions.stem: The leak check still fails after the breathing circuit is swapped. Where should you look next?
options: The hospital pipeline supply and zone valves
The O2 flush valve and its spring return
Low-pressure parts: absorber housing and vaporizer seals
The patient's ETT cuff and pilot balloon
questions.explanation: Swapping the circuit usually fixes a failed leak check. If it still fails, the leak is in the machine: the absorber (screws, gaskets, granules, petcock) and vaporizers (mounts, seals, fill ports) are common sites.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slides 19, 22 (PDF p. 10, 11); CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 13 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: On this desflurane vaporizer schematic, which numbered component does the provider adjust with the dial?
questions.explanation: Component 2 is the variable resistance controlled by the anesthetist through the vaporizer dial. Component 1 is the valve controlled by the differential pressure transducer (3), and 4 is the fixed resistance in the diluent (fresh gas) path.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 61, 62 (PDF p. 31)

questions.stem: Which sequence traces pipeline O2 to the common gas outlet?
options: Pipeline inlet check valve, flowmeter, second-stage regulator, vaporizer, flow control valve, outlet check valve
Pipeline inlet check valve, first-stage regulator, flowmeter, flow control valve, vaporizer, outlet check valve
Second-stage regulator, pipeline inlet check valve, vaporizer, flowmeter, flow control valve, outlet check valve
Pipeline inlet check valve, second-stage regulator, flow control valve, flowmeter, vaporizer, outlet check valve
questions.explanation: Pipeline gas enters the intermediate system through the inlet check valve (no first-stage regulator; that's for cylinders), passes the second-stage regulator and flow control valve, then the low-pressure flowmeter, vaporizer, outlet check valve, and CGO.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 5, 31, 33 (PDF p. 3, 16, 17)

questions.stem: After construction, N2O is found flowing through the O2 pipeline. Supply pressure is normal. Which statement is correct?
options: Neither fail-safe nor proportioner acts; only the O2 analyzer shows it
The fail-safe valve senses the N2O and stops its flow
The O2 supply low-pressure alarm sounds right away
The proportioning system raises O2 flow to compensate
questions.explanation: Crossed pipelines are an upstream hypoxemia hazard. The fail-safe senses pressure (normal here), and the proportioner links the flowmeter settings, not gas identity. Only the inspired O2 analyzer shows the falling FiO2; then disconnect the pipeline and open the cylinder.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 34, 45, 46 (PDF p. 17, 23); Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 19 (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: The machine's O2 pipeline gauge reads 20 psig because the hose is kinked behind the machine, but no O2 supply alarm sounds. The cylinder was left open. Why is there no alarm?
options: The alarm monitors only N2O supply pressure
The open cylinder is holding supply pressure near 45 psi
The alarm sounds only when pressure reaches 0 psig
The fail-safe valve silences the O2 alarm
questions.explanation: With the cylinder open, the machine draws from it as soon as pipeline pressure falls below the regulated ~45 psi, so supply pressure stays up and no alarm sounds until the cylinder empties. That's the lecture's reason to close the cylinder after the check.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 4 (PDF p. 2); Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 33 (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: For a 3-hour case at 2.5% sevo on 2 L/min fresh gas, what liquid volume is used?
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 52 (PDF p. 26)

questions.stem: Which pairings of adjunct and complication are correct? Select 2.
options: NPA: lip trauma from the flange
questions.explanation: NPA's most common complication is epistaxis. OPA complications are lip and tongue trauma, dental damage, and stimulation of oropharyngeal and laryngeal reflexes.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slides 5, 6 (PDF p. 5, 6)

questions.stem: What does the vaporizer interlock mechanism (push button, then turn counterclockwise) accomplish?
options: It locks the filler port closed while the vaporizer is in use
It prevents tipping while the vaporizer is being transported
It prevents accidental activation and more than one vaporizer on
It compensates vaporizer output for changes in temperature
questions.explanation: The interlock requires deliberate action to open the dial from its locked position, and the manifold system allows only one vaporizer on at a time. Transport (T) mode is what protects against tipping leaks.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 59 (PDF p. 30)

questions.stem: O2 supply pressure dips to 35 psig with N2O running. What does the fail-safe do?
options: It stops N2O flow completely right away
It proportionally reduces N2O flow now
It raises O2 flow to compensate for the dip
Nothing yet; it acts below about 25-30 psig
questions.explanation: The fail-safe begins proportionally reducing other gases below about 25-30 psig and stops them below about 20. At 35 psig it hasn't engaged, though the supply alarm may warn you.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 34 (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: During a tonsillectomy, the uncuffed ETT has a large leak, and the gas mix is 50% O2 / 50% N2O. The surgeon is using cautery in the oropharynx. Which change most reduces fire risk?
options: Increase O2 to 100% to protect saturation
Increase fresh gas flow to dilute the leak
Replace N2O with air and use the lowest FiO2 tolerated
questions.explanation: The leak creates an oxidizer-rich oropharynx next to the ignition source. 50/50 O2/N2O supports combustion like 100% O2; lowering oxidizer means air with minimal FiO2 and no N2O.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slides 33, 35 (PDF p. 17, 18); Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 9 (PDF p. 9)

questions.stem: After a heated humidifier is added to the circuit, the bag can't be squeezed and no gas reaches the patient. What is the likely cause?
options: A closed O2 cylinder valve on the machine
An APL valve left fully open to the scavenger
An incorrectly connected humidifier occluding the circuit
questions.explanation: Incorrectly connected humidifiers are among the reported causes of total circuit occlusion (with filters, defects, and plastic wrap). High resistance with no flow = occlusion.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 22 (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: An O2 E-cylinder reads 300 psig. How long will it support a non-rebreather at 10 L/min?
questions.explanation: 300/1900 × 660 ≈ 104 L. 104 ÷ 10 ≈ 10 minutes: replace the cylinder before transport.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 13 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: During mask ventilation, condensation in the clear mask comes and goes with each squeeze, and SpO2 is stable. What does the fog tell you?
options: Gas is moving in and out of the airway
The circuit humidity is too high
questions.explanation: A clear mask lets you watch condensation from exhalation; instructor note: pay attention to the quantity of fog. Cyclic fogging means exhaled gas is reaching the mask.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 4 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: According to the lecture, what did the widespread use of electrocautery hasten?
options: Replacement of cuffed tubes with uncuffed tubes
Use of N2O as a carrier gas
Elimination of explosive anesthetic agents from the OR
Adoption of isolated power in homes
questions.explanation: Widespread ESU use hastened the elimination of explosive agents from the OR, since a high-energy ignition source can't coexist with flammable anesthetics.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 31 (PDF p. 16)

questions.stem: For a sevoflurane mask induction, which step best limits waste gas before the mask is sealed on the face?
options: Squeeze the bag to empty the circuit first
Keep the APL fully closed until the mask is applied
Don't start fresh gas and agent flowing until the mask is sealed
Run high FGF to prefill the circuit with agent while positioning
questions.explanation: Gas flowing while the circuit is open to the room is a technique error; 94-99% of OR contamination comes from technique. Prefilling at high flow with the mask off, or emptying the bag into the room, spills agent.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 14 (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: A 250 mL bottle of sevoflurane is used at 2% with 2 L/min FGF. About how many hours will it last?
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 52 (PDF p. 26)

questions.stem: The expiratory unidirectional valve disc is missing. What happens to exhaled gas?
options: It bypasses the absorber into the inspiratory limb only
Some flows back from the expiratory limb and is reinhaled
It's all vented through the APL
questions.explanation: Missing or incompetent unidirectional valves are a hypercarbia hazard. Without the expiratory valve, exhaled gas can move back toward the patient on inspiration and be rebreathed.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 20 (PDF p. 10); CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 8 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: In a Thorpe tube, why does more flow push the float higher?
options: Flowing gas warms and expands the float at high flows
Pressure across the float rises in proportion to flow
The float gets lighter as more gas flows around it
The float rises to a wider section where the gap passes that flow
questions.explanation: The tube is tapered, narrow at the bottom. The pressure drop across the float stays constant (gravity balance), so more flow lifts it to a wider section where the larger annular orifice passes that flow: constant pressure, variable orifice.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 42, 43 (PDF p. 21, 22)

questions.stem: Why must desflurane be delivered at 2 atm and 39 °C rather than from a standard vaporizer?
options: It forms compound A unless the vaporizer is heated
Its low vapor pressure needs heat before it will evaporate
Its high blood:gas coefficient requires heated delivery
Its boiling point near room temperature makes output unpredictable
questions.explanation: Des boils at 22.8 °C with a vapor pressure of 669 mmHg. At room temperature it could boil in a standard sump and swing output widely. Heating and pressurizing makes delivery predictable. Its blood:gas coefficient (0.42) is the lowest listed.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 60 (PDF p. 30)

questions.stem: For a prone posterior fossa craniotomy with the neck sharply flexed, which tube is chosen and why?
options: Uncuffed tube, to reduce tracheal pressure
Oral RAE, because it routes the connector over the chin
Armored tube, because it resists kinking and compression
questions.explanation: Armored (reinforced) tubes resist kinking and compression in head, neck, and tracheal surgery and awkward positions. RAE tubes exist to route the connector away from the surgical field.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 8 (PDF p. 8)

questions.stem: Which systems physically prevent connecting the wrong gas source to the machine? Select 2.
questions.explanation: PISS (cylinder to yoke) and DISS (pipeline to machine) use gas-specific geometry. The fail-safe and proportioner protect against low O2 pressure and low O2 ratios, not wrong connections.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slides 18, 29 (PDF p. 9, 15)

questions.stem: During laser surgery, why is the laser tube's cuff filled with saline or water rather than air?
options: The cuff itself isn't laser resistant
Saline keeps the cuff pressure lower
questions.explanation: The laser-resistant tube shaft is noncombustible, but its cuff isn't laser resistant. Filling it with saline or water (with dye) is the lecture's precaution.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 9 (PDF p. 9)

questions.stem: On these unlabeled cylinder valves, which numbered valve would fit a medical air yoke (pins 1 and 5)?
questions.explanation: Air uses positions 1 and 5 (valve 3). Valve 4 shares position 1 but pairs it with 6 (carbon dioxide); its right hole sits farther out. Valve 2 is N2O (3,5) and valve 5 is Entonox (7).
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 7 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: Using the lecture's fire triad at the cylinder yoke, how does opening a new cylinder valve slowly lower fire risk?
options: It removes the oxidizer from inside the cylinder
It lowers the cylinder's fill pressure over time
It limits heat from gas rushing through the outlet
It lets dust on the yoke burn off harmlessly
questions.explanation: At the yoke, O2 or N2O is the oxidizer, dust is the fuel, and compressed gas rushing through the outlet creates heat. Opening slowly reduces that heat; clearing dust removes the fuel.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia (Elmore): slide 8 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: In this circle system, suppose the fresh gas inflow were moved into quadrant C, between the patient and the expiratory valve. What would happen?
options: Fresh gas would leave via the expiratory limb, bypassing the patient
Nothing; fresh gas can safely enter anywhere in the circle
The absorber would be bypassed, raising compound A levels
The APL valve would stop venting waste gas to the scavenger
questions.explanation: Quadrant C is the expiratory limb on the patient side. The hazards lecture lists a fresh gas inlet between the patient and the expiratory valve as one of three arrangements to avoid: fresh gas leaves with exhaled gas instead of reaching the patient.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 8 (PDF p. 4); Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 20 (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: During a power failure, a colleague assumes every monitor in the room is running on the anesthesia machine's battery. Why is that assumption unsafe?
options: The battery powers monitors only after the ventilator stops
All monitors shut off as soon as AC power is lost
The battery powers only the vaporizers and flowmeters
Monitors, alarms, and the ventilator may not share one power source
questions.explanation: The lecture says to know exactly what runs on battery alone: monitors, airway monitors, BP and HR, alarms, and the ventilator may or may not be tied to the same power source.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 25 (PDF p. 13)

questions.stem: Why does the absorber add little heat and humidity benefit during a 10 L/min fresh gas flow case?
options: The absorbent stops reacting chemically at high flow
Heat conservation occurs only with desflurane use
Large volumes of cool, dry fresh gas dilute the conserved heat
High flow desiccates the absorbent within minutes
questions.explanation: Exhaled heat and humidity are partially conserved by the absorbent, and both are optimized as flow decreases. At high FGF, the circuit fills with dry, room-temperature medical gas instead.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 8 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: For a spontaneously breathing transport patient, which numbered circuits need the HIGHER fresh gas flow (1.5-2.5 × MV)? Select 2.
options: Only the one with the longest tubing
questions.explanation: Circuits 2 and 3 are Mapleson B and C: fresh gas enters near the patient and they always permit rebreathing, so they need 1.5-2.5 × MV. Circuit 1 is the Mapleson A, efficient for spontaneous breathing at 0.7 × MV.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 21 (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: A clear canister shows a purple streak running along the wall while the center granules stay white. Which statements are correct? Select 2.
options: The white center means the whole canister is safe
Gas is channeling along the canister wall
The streak shows regeneration after rest
The canister is evenly used and has plenty of capacity
Channeling increases resistance across the canister
The streaked path may be exhausted even though most granules look fresh
questions.explanation: Channeling sends gas preferentially along the smooth wall, exhausting that path while other granules look unused, one reason color isn't trusted. Channeling follows the path of least resistance; it doesn't raise it.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slides 4, 5 (PDF p. 2, 3)

questions.stem: On their first day, a new SRNA sets up an unfamiliar workstation model and misses a disconnected hose. Which aggravating factors apply? Select 2.
questions.explanation: A new provider on a new model combines inexperience with lack of familiarity with equipment. Nothing in the scenario suggests fatigue or time pressure, and connectors and alarms are protective.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 18 (PDF p. 9)

questions.stem: The pop-off (APL) valve in this circle sits in quadrant D. Moving it into which quadrant would violate the circle arrangement rules?
options: None; the APL can go anywhere
questions.explanation: Quadrant B is the inspiratory limb on the patient side, between the patient and the inspiratory valve. An APL there is one of the three forbidden arrangements: it would vent fresh gas before it reaches the patient.
questions.citation: CO2 Absorbents and Scavenging (McPherson): slide 8 (PDF p. 4); Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 20 (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: During mask ventilation, which findings can you assess directly through a clear face mask? Select 3.
questions.explanation: The clear mask lets you see lip color, condensation from exhalation, secretions, vomitus, and blood. Tidal volume, ETCO2, and SpO2 come from monitors, not from looking through the mask.
questions.citation: Airway Equipment (McPherson): slide 4 (PDF p. 4)

questions.stem: A committee reviews how often machine-check failures have occurred over two years before deciding on new training. Which risk management step is this?
options: Monitoring after a change is made
questions.explanation: Steps: define problems → estimate likelihood → weigh the benefits of expending resources → apply solutions → monitor. Measuring how often a problem happens is estimating likelihood.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slide 16 (PDF p. 8)

questions.stem: During MAC with O2 by nasal cannula near the surgical field, which numbered element of this fire triangle is the anesthesia provider's main lever?
options: None; fire prevention is the surgeon's job
questions.explanation: Element 2 is the oxidizer (O2), which anesthesia controls: keep FiO2 as low as tolerated, avoid N2O, and keep O2 from pooling. Element 1 (ignition, the cautery) belongs to the surgeon and element 3 (fuel) mostly to nursing, though prevention is everyone's job.
questions.citation: Anesthesia Workstation Hazards & Safety (McPherson): slides 33, 35 (PDF p. 17, 18)
